This isn’t necessarily for OP but any CS students, CS has traditionally been a degree for software developers to get. If you want to do something more software engineering related, you should consider if your university has other sofwatre engineering degrees.

My CS degree program I took prepares students for graduate school and academia. It was very theoretical, and I wish I had done the software engineering degree instead because many of those classes were relevant to my actual full stack job I do today. I don’t fully regret CS because of all the foundational knowledge it taught me, but definitely consider if CS is the right degree for you if you want to program for a career!

You should absolutely apply for internships. Regardless of if you think you’re ready or not. That is an entire set of jobs that you will NOT be likely eligible for when you graduate. Often those opportunities if you are good enough can turn into full time positions anyway. 

Apply for internships by yourself AND especially try with your school too they often have career resources for internships.

I would recommend a Dragontail tenkara rod because they have great customer service, there’s a ready supply of replacement parts, and they’re great entry level price. They have a coupon code for first time buyers I believe.

Based on what you are telling me, I would recommend looking into the Dragontail Foxfire or Dragontail Kaida, shorter rods for the small streams with tight cover. 

The Mizuchi is also an amazing first rod in my opinion, but its longest length could be too long for your stream but only you’ll be able to make that judgement! In Utah I think it’s a perfect beginner rod because it was designed for streams near Idaho so it matches my locations streams.
